assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy is a coherent arc from hormone biology to drugs that have transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity care, with additional cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality, clarity and breadth of impact on patients are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Holst (incretin physiology, bioactive GLP-1 forms), Drucker (GLP-1 biology, intestinotrophic GLP-2, translation) and Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1 peptide) form a defensible trio. Lotte Bjerre Knudsen (liraglutide/semaglutide design) is a strong alternative; Joel Habener is not in the credited list, so the allocation is genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and very large outcome trials; the interpretation is stable. Timing is ripe given the clinical scale.
uncertainties: Whether peptide chemistry/drug design (Knudsen) should displace a discovery-side laureate.
Credit for the discovery of the active GLP-1 peptide is disputed and I cannot verify the details independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a dominant driver of synovial inflammation and that its blockade produces durable clinical benefit established the cytokine-targeted paradigm for chronic inflammatory disease, with lasting impact across rheumatoid arthritis, IBD and psoriasis. From a clinical autoimmunity vantage it is a clear translational milestone.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini led the translation from the human synovial cytokine-network work to the anti-TNF trials, a clean two-person configuration. Contributions of antibody developers and others are real but secondary to the proof of concept.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of use, biosimilars and robust confirmation. Recognition is mature and not premature.
uncertainties: Whether a basic TNF-biology contribution outside the credited names would be expected in a fair configuration.
Possible view that this is therapeutic development more than a discovery of fundamental mechanism.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cytosolic DNA sensing through cGAS, the second messenger cGAMP and STING is a fundamental innate-immunity mechanism that connects infection, interferonopathies, autoimmunity (including lupus-like disease), cancer immunity and senescence. Highly original and conceptually clear.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and cGAMP, and Barber identified STING; these are the decisive contributions. Ishikawa shares STING credit, and Sun and Wu worked in Chen's laboratory, so the allocation of the STING credit is somewhat open.
assessment.maturity: The mechanism is confirmed independently in many systems. Clinical translation (STING agonists and inhibitors) is still immature, but the basic discovery is ready for recognition.
uncertainties: Therapeutic impact is not yet established.
Distribution of STING credit between Barber and Ishikawa.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells have produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new treatment modality. Impact is major and originality high, and the work builds on the T-cell biology that the committee has recently honored.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical CD19 CAR-T with 4-1BB), Sadelain (CD28 costimulated CARs and the preclinical foundation) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer, TIL, early gene-engineered T cells) are credited. Earlier CAR concepts (Eshhar, Kuwana) are not in the credited list, which complicates priority.
assessment.maturity: Approved products and long-term follow-up exist. Remaining limitations are solid tumors, toxicity and relapse, but for B-cell malignancies the effect is established.
uncertainties: Priority for the chimeric receptor concept is not in the supplied credit.
Whether the proper recognition belongs to the cell-engineering or the clinical-translation contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defining the thymus as the site of T-cell development and the bursa-derived origin of B cells established the two-lineage organization of adaptive immunity, foundational to all later immunology and to understanding immunodeficiency and autoimmunity.
assessment.attribution: Miller (thymus function) and Cooper (B-cell lineage and the dual-system concept, with Good) is a natural pairing. Robert Good and others who contributed to the early work are not in the credited list, and I cannot verify details of the early priority.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed and textbook-level for decades. The question is not maturity but whether the recognition has been overtaken by timing.
uncertainties: Contributions of deceased colleagues cannot be recognized.
Age and availability of the living laureates is an unresolved timing concern.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Light-gated control of genetically defined cells transformed experimental neuroscience and physiology and enabled causal circuit dissection across species. Very high methodological impact, with limited direct clinical use so far.
assessment.attribution: Credit is split across the discovery of channelrhodopsin (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg), its first use in neurons (Boyden, Deisseroth) and earlier genetic photostimulation concepts (Miesenböck). Any three-person configuration leaves out meritorious contributors.
assessment.maturity: Broadly confirmed and in universal use. Retinal clinical applications are emerging, but a tool-based recognition is clearly timely.
uncertainties: Contested allocation among six credited names.
Whether the prize emphasis should be on the discovery of the channel or on neuronal application.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cloning and characterization of IL-6 as a B-cell differentiation factor and its role in inflammation, together with therapeutic blockade of the receptor (tocilizumab), links a basic cytokine discovery to treatment of rheumatoid arthritis, giant cell arteritis, cytokine-release syndrome and other conditions.
assessment.attribution: Kishimoto and Hirano are the decisive discoverers of the cytokine, and Kishimoto drove the receptor-blocking antibody development. The two-person configuration is clear.
assessment.maturity: Long clinical record and consistent confirmation; recognition is timely though overlapping with the TNF paradigm.
uncertainties: Overlap in concept with TNF blockade could argue for only one cytokine-therapy prize.
Part of the therapeutic credit lies with the antibody engineering team, not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-switching antisense oligonucleotide therapy for spinal muscular atrophy converted a lethal pediatric disease into a treatable one and established a general paradigm for RNA-targeted drugs. Originality and patient impact are strong.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (mechanistic splicing work and the SMN2 exon 7 target) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and nusinersen development) form a clean two-person configuration. Contributions from other splicing and SMN groups are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Approved in 2016 with years of real-world follow-up, although the broader antisense field is still developing and long-term outcomes are being collected.
uncertainties: Competition from other SMA therapies (gene therapy, small molecules) in assessing the singular importance.
Whether the field is mature enough compared with older candidates.
